what_its_for: Betaine is used to treat a rare inherited condition called homocystinuria. This condition causes a buildup of a substance called homocysteine in your blood and urine, which can lead to problems with your bones, eyes, blood vessels, and brain. Betaine helps lower the levels of homocysteine in your body to reduce these risks.
how_to_take: Betaine comes as a powder that you mix with liquid before taking. Measure the prescribed amount of powder using the scoop provided. Mix it with 4 to 6 ounces (about half a cup) of water, juice, or milk and stir until it is completely dissolved. Take it right away after mixing — do not let it sit. Take betaine with meals. Always use the measuring scoop that comes with your bottle and replace the cap tightly after each use.
dosing: The dose is different for each person and is based on your weight and lab results. A common starting dose for adults and children over 3 years old is 3 grams (one scoop) taken twice a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose based on your blood test results. Children under 3 years old are usually started at 100 mg per kilogram of body weight per day, split into two doses. Never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store betaine powder at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the bottle tightly closed to protect the powder from moisture. Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep out of reach of children. Once you open the bottle, use the powder within 3 months. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods or beverages you must strictly avoid while taking betaine. However, you should continue to follow any special low-methionine diet your doctor has recommended, as diet is an important part of managing homocystinuria. Talk to your doctor before starting any new vitamins, supplements, or medications, as some may interact with betaine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience sudden severe headache, vision changes, nausea, vomiting, or confusion — these could be signs of a dangerous buildup of a substance called methionine. Also call your doctor if you notice swelling of the brain symptoms such as difficulty thinking clearly, loss of balance, or unusual behavior. Contact your doctor if you feel your condition is not improving or if you have any new or worsening symptoms. Seek emergency help immediately if you have signs of a stroke such as sudden numbness, trouble speaking, or weakness on one side of your body.
when_it_works: Betaine starts lowering homocysteine levels in your blood within a few weeks of starting treatment. However, you may not feel any different right away, because this medicine works quietly in the background to reduce your risk of serious complications over time. Your doctor will check your blood levels regularly to make sure the medicine is working properly. It is very important to keep taking betaine every day, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before using betaine, as it is not fully known how it may affect an unborn baby or nursing infant. Children can take betaine and doses are carefully adjusted by weight. Older adults can use betaine but should be monitored closely by their doctor. People with kidney disease or other serious health conditions should inform their doctor, as dose adjustments may be needed.
